'lt is a long time since FP have been so delighted with an article of food as we have been recently with a cus- tard made from " Eiffel Tower " Custard Powder. It is simply perfect, and we advise every lover of Custard to try it at once. We recommend it simply and solely for its excellence, at the same time we cannot under- stand how the makers can produce for a penny a packet sufficient to make a quart. You can doubtless get it from your Grocer, but WP understand that Messrs. Foster, Clark and Co., 3796 " Eiffel Tower "Factory, Maidstone (who are also manufactir era of the famous "Effel Tower "Lemonade) will send sufficient to make a quart free on receipt of a postcard.

div.head: OUR LOCAL CHURCHES. Bold-street Wesleyan Church.—Sunday School Anniversary Services.
div.p: OUR LOCAL CHURCHES. Bold-street Wesleyan Church.—Sun- day School Anniversary Services.

The Rev J Ho well Jone of Bolton. and formerly of 1 the Warrington circuit, was the nreacher at the anni- versary services in cotnection with Bold-street Wesleyan Sunday chool which were held in the church on Sunday. At the morning service the rev gentleman took for the subject of his sermon, " Child training." the example being the life nf Moses. Special hymns were rendered by the choir and children, who had been specially trained, and the manner in which the hymns were su 1-i-fleeted the greatest credit on the teachers and others, no pains having evidently ber n spared to make the musical portion of the service as attractive as possible. The choir rendered the anthem," As pants the hart " (Spohr), in a creditable manner, the solo part being taken by Miss Ida Kirkham. Ie the afternoon a special children's service was held, when the members of the Bewsey-road and Ellesmere-street schools were present. The chairman WaS Mr J G Wlthinshaw, of Penketh, who delivend a short address on "The power of example." Miss Emily Taylor effectively sang "Sun of my soul," and a praiseworthy rendition of the flute solo, " With verdure clad," was given hy Mr W H Podmore. An address was delivered by Mr R Posnett, of Runcorn, who spoke upon "The mystery of growth." Another solo "Arm, arm, ye brave," was rendered by Mr E H Pearse. At the evening service the seating capacity of the chapel was taxed to the utmost, forms having to be placed in the gallery. A powerful sermon was preached by Mr Jones upon " A shipwreck and its les ons." The anthem, "The day thou gayest," was rendered by the choir, and the solo " Hear ye, Israel," was contributed by Miss Kirkham. Great praise is due to Mr Frank Hickman for his efficient services at the organ. The collections for the day, which were on behalf of the Sunday school funds,arnounted :o the sum of £5O 2c.Bd.

div.head: FOOTBALL.
div.p: FOOTBALL.

The Northern Union. The Establishment of the League Confirmed. On Tueeday night there was a largely attended meeting of toe General Committee ot tne Northern Rugby Union at the George Hotel, iluddertflnid, under the chairmanship of Mr El Hutchinson, of Wakefield. Twenty- hreo delezates were present. . .

The question of the formation of the Northern League led to a long and animated discussion. Its formation was ultimately confirmed by 12 votes to 11. Leigh and Brighouse, who bad formerly been oppt s:d to the for- mation, having gone over to the other side.

.. • :aThe bye-laws, which had been agreed to by the clubs in the League, were brought up and adopted by the Maim]. These provide that there shall be an entrance fee of £5 5s and an annual subscription of £5 53 and that the competition be limited to fourteen clubs, to be in membership with and under the authority of the Northern Uni m. The management is to vest in a com- mittee of one representative of each club in the corn- p.tition, from which committee the officers are to be chosen five members of the committee to form a quorum at the meeting. Travelling expenses of representatives are to be paid out of League funds. Alterations or res cinding of rules must be carried by two-thirds of the commiM e present, after three weeks' notice- The committee are empowered to deal with offending clubs or players, and any other matter arising not pro- vided for in the byelaws. All matches must be played under rhe laws of the N-Irthern Union, and be of 80 minutes duration, but if less than 60 minutes the com- mittee are empowered to declare the same no League match. No club or official shall be allowed to declare a Leagued match off and play a non-League match in- stead. The points counted are two for a win, one for a draw, the highest club to be champion. Clubs tieing for championship or toe bottom position are to play off, and the proceeds to bo at the disposal of the committee A challenge cup is to be competed for, with gold medals for the champion team. Players to be entitled to medals inust have played in at least six matches. rhe club having the lowest number of points at the end of the season shall retire from the League, and its place be taken by the winner of a test match between the accredited champiens of the Lancashire and Yorkshire Senior Com- petitions. The club retiring from the League shall the following season be included in the Senior Competition of the coun:y to which such club belongs. Any club guilty of a breach of the professional laws shall have two points deducted from its score. The Union deli• gate to the League Committee power to decide all questions of qualifications, broken engagements, fixing of dates for matches which can not be mutually a. ranged, protests, disputes and complaints, champion- ship affairs, and transfers. At the same time the Union reserve to themselves the right on appeal to over-ride decisions of the League. The League will c nne into operation at the com- mencement of next season.

A Violent Husband.—Separation Oider
Granted

Thomas Fairbrother—, 1-I.,.l37l.gewater-street, was Charged at the Borough Police Court on Wednesday before Mr Geddes and Alderman Heaton, with having assaulted his wife Mary l'airbrother on Tuesday.—Complainant said that on Tuesday morn- ing prisoner was very abusive and kicked and thumped her, He said he was not going to keep ter, nor her children.—Pi isoner was sent to gaol for a month with hard labour. A separation order was granted, the wife to have lOs per week and the custody of the children.

Presentation to the Rev. W. Bracecamp, The Rev W Bracecamp (curate of Sc. Peter's Parish) was the recipient on Monday evening of silver purse containing £2O from the members oft the congregation and friends, in recognition of his valuable services during the prolonged absence through illne.s of the Vicar (the Rev. B. Percival.) The interesting proceedings took place in the schoolroom, John-street, and there was a crowded attendance: The presenta- tion was a spontaneous effort on the part of the congregation, aud it is only a fortnight since the idea was mooted.—The Vicar (Rev B Percival) made the presentation, which consisted of £29 in cash, on behalf of the congregation and paid a tribute to the zealous services of Mr Brace- camp.—Mr Bracecarap suitably acknow;e,iged the gift, and referred to the great assistance he had received, during the Vicar's absence, from Mrs Percival.
